title: Clesrovimab, a monoclonal antibody for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus disease in infants: a drug profile.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in young children. In children < 5 years old, it causes an estimated 33 million LRTI episodes and over 100,000 deaths annually, two-thirds of which occur in infants. The licensure of new long-acting monoclonal antibodies and a maternal RSV vaccine offer opportunities for reducing RSV related infant morbidity and mortality. AREAS COVERED: This drug profile reviews clesrovimab (Enflonsia, Merck & Co. Rahway, NJ U.S.A.), an extended half-life human IgG1κ monoclonal antibody, targeting the highly conserved antigenic site IV of the RSV fusion protein. We synthesize evidence from phase 1 to phase 3 clinical trials, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data, regulatory approvals and resistance profiling, drawing on peer-reviewed literature and regulatory sources available until May 2026. EXPERT OPINION: Clesrovimab offers a single, fixed-dose, weight-independent injection per RSV season, with demonstrated safety and efficacy against medically attended RSV disease and hospitalization in infants. Its epitope target is distinct from that of nirsevimab (site Ø) and no cross resistance between the two antibodies has been observed in vitro. Equitable global access to monoclonal antibodies, particularly for low- and middle-income countries, remains critical to reduce the global RSV burden.

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus in association with environmental factors: A systematic review.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus are the leading causes of respiratory morbidity and mortality globally. Environmental factors influence the spread of these diseases, yet considerable variation remains in how these relationships are modelled across different climates and geographic scales. This systematic review evaluates the use of spatiotemporal frameworks to investigate the relationship between environmental factors and these diseases. STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus identified peer-reviewed studies investigating the relationship between environmental factors and influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus using spatiotemporal modelling approaches. Methodological quality was assessed using the Spatial Methodology Appraisal of Research Tool. This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. RESULTS: Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Temperature and humidity were the most identified environmental determinants. Bayesian hierarchical models were the leading analytical framework for handling spatial and temporal dependencies. The interaction between environmental factors and area-level socioeconomic conditions significantly influenced local infection risk. Overall, the findings indicate that these relationships are often nonlinear and vary across locations, with threshold effects and geographical heterogeneity frequently reported. CONCLUSIONS: Spatiotemporal modelling is a valuable tool for investigating the associations between environmental factors and respiratory infection risk. The reviewed evidence suggests that these relationships are often complex, delayed, and, in some cases, nonlinear. This study highlights temperature and humidity as the main environmental factors influencing respiratory infections, noting that local socioeconomic conditions strongly shape their impact. Effective public health surveillance should incorporate localised environmental characteristics and socioeconomic vulnerabilities to better address disease risk across diverse areas.

source_records.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus are the leading causes of respiratory morbidity and mortality globally. Environmental factors influence the spread of these diseases, yet considerable variation remains in how these relationships are modelled across different climates and geographic scales. This systematic review evaluates the use of spatiotemporal frameworks to investigate the relationship between environmental factors and these diseases. STUDY DESIGN: Systematic review. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus identified peer-reviewed studies investigating the relationship between environmental factors and influenza, pneumonia, and respiratory syncytial virus using spatiotemporal modelling approaches. Methodological quality was assessed using the Spatial Methodology Appraisal of Research Tool. This review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. RESULTS: Twelve studies met the inclusion criteria. Temperature and humidity were the most identified environmental determinants. The interaction between environmental factors and area-level socioeconomic conditions significantly influenced local infection risk. The reviewed evidence suggests that these relationships are often complex, delayed, and, in some cases, nonlinear. This study highlights temperature and humidity as the main environmental factors influencing respiratory infections, noting that local socioeconomic conditions strongly shape their impact. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 流感、肺炎和 呼吸道合胞病毒 是全球呼吸道疾病和 呼吸道合胞病毒 的主要原因。环境因素影响这些疾病的传播,但在不同气候和地理范围内建模这些关系的方式仍然存在很大差异。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本系统综述评估了时空框架的使用,以研究环境因素与这些疾病之间的关系。该研究设计是对同行评审研究的系统回顾,这些研究使用时空建模方法来检查环境因素与呼吸道感染之间的关系。
elements_zh.methods: 对 PubMed、Embase 和 Scopus 的系统检索确定了使用时空建模方法调查环境因素与流感、肺炎和 呼吸道合胞病毒 之间关系的同行评审研究。使用研究工具的空间方法学评估来评估方法学质量。该综述遵循系统评价和荟萃分析的首选报告项目 (PRISMA) 2020 指南,并已在 PROSPERO 注册。
elements_zh.main_results: 十二项研究符合纳入标准。温度和湿度是最确定的环境决定因素。贝叶斯分层模型是处理空间和时间依赖性的领先分析框架。环境因素和地区社会经济条件之间的相互作用显着影响当地感染风险。总体而言,研究结果表明,这些关系通常是非线性的,并且因地点而异,经常报告阈值效应和地理异质性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 审查的证据表明,这些关系通常是复杂的、延迟的,并且在某些情况下是非线性的。这项研究强调温度和湿度是影响呼吸道感染的主要环境因素,并指出当地的社会经济条件对其影响有很大影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 有效的公共卫生 监测 应结合当地的环境特征和社会经济脆弱性,以更好地应对不同地区的疾病风险。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据没有报告与研究设计或数据质量相关的具体限制。证据强度中等,因为研究结果是基于对现有研究的系统回顾而不是原始数据。

title: The epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in hospitalized children in Europe before the widespread implementation of new RSV prophylactic strategies: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric respiratory infections. This systematic review and meta-analysis aims to estimate the in-hospital positivity among children in Europe post-COVID-19 and prior to the implementation of the recent RSV prophylactic strategies. A systematic search was conducted across three databases: PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science from 01/01/2021-31/12/2025. Studies enrolling children aged 0-18 years who were hospitalized with respiratory infection and detected positive for RSV were eligible for inclusion. A random-effect model was applied and heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 statistics. Thirty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria, encompasing 66,065 children. The overall pooled RSV in-hospital positivity was 48% (95%CI: 41%-56%). Positivity estimates per year were: 53% (95%CI:49%-56%) for 2021-2022, 49% (95%CI:36%-62%) for 2022-2023, and 62% (95%CI:51%-73%) for 2023-2024 (p = 0.308). RSV positivity in studies with infants (<12-months-old) was 69% vs 30% in studies including older children (0-18 years). Among RSV-positive patients, co-infections were detected in 17%, respiratory support was required in 62% and ICU/NICU admission in 11%. RSV-B predominated over RSV-A during the study period. A substantial burden of RSV-related hospitalizations was detected, especially in infants < 12-months-old; however, the overall pooled positivity estimate should be interpreted with caution. These findings provide an important pre-immunization baseline for evaluating the impact of maternal RSV vaccination and monoclonal antibodies and support the need for continued RSV surveillance across Europe.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis assesses the in-hospital positivity of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in European children before the implementation of new prophylactic strategies. The study included 38 eligible studies with 66,065 children, reporting an overall pooled RSV positivity of 48% (95%CI: 41%-56%). Positivity varied by year, with 53% in 2021-2022, 49% in 2022-2023, and 62% in 2023-2024. RSV-B was more prevalent than RSV-A. Infants had higher positivity rates (69%) compared to older children (30%). Co-infections were detected in 17% of RSV-positive cases, with 62% requiring respiratory support and 11% needing ICU/NICU admission. The findings highlight the burden of RSV-related hospitalizations, especially in infants, and underscore the importance of continued surveillance and the evaluation of new interventions.

title: Nirsevimab for respiratory syncytial virus prevention: A comprehensive product review.
abstract: Infant RSV prevention is undergoing a public-health paradigm shift toward scalable, broad-eligibility passive immunization. This review examines nirsevimab (Beyfortus®), a long-acting recombinant IgG1κ monoclonal antibody targeting the conserved site Ø of prefusion RSV F protein. Its extended half-life enables season-long protection with a single dose, overcoming key limitations of palivizumab. A validated manufacturing platform and stringent release specifications ensure consistent quality and potency. title: Development and evaluation of an ARTIC-based amplicon sequencing assay for whole-genome characterization of respiratory syncytial virus.
abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a ~15.2 kb negative-sense RNA virus, causes acute respiratory infections in infants and older adults. Its two subtypes, RSV-A and RSV-B, evolve rapidly, making ongoing monitoring of circulating strains essential. The Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) developed and evaluated an amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing (WGS) assay for RSV surveillance. A total of 214 de-identified remnant clinical specimens (102 RSV-A and 112 RSV-B) with RT-PCR C q values <31 were included. RSV genomes were amplified using ARTIC-style and custom primer sets, with the ARTIC set showing superior performance. Libraries were prepared using a modified Illumina COVIDSeq protocol, sequenced on NextSeq 1000/2000 instruments, and analyzed using the GPHL-RSV-PIPE bioinformatics pipeline. Among genomes meeting validation criteria, sequencing depth was slightly higher for RSV-A (median 53,433×; mean 51,076×) than RSV-B (median 49,699×; mean 46,945×), whereas genomic coverage was slightly lower for RSV-A (median 97.5%; mean 96.6%) than RSV-B (median 98.3%; mean 97.6%). Predominant lineages were A.D.3.1 and A.D.5.2 for RSV-A and B.D.E.1 for RSV-B. For RSV-A, the assay showed 92.8% accuracy, 96.2% sensitivity, 87.2% specificity, 92.6% positive predictive value, and 93.2% negative predictive value. Intra- and inter-run precision assessed using 16 and 53-57 genomes, respectively, showed nearly 100% consensus genome identity with 0–5 nucleotide differences. Specificity testing of 31 non-RSV specimens produced no false-positive detections. Limits of detection were 4.4 TCID 50 /mL for RSV-A and 18.6 TCID 50 /mL for RSV-B. These results demonstrate that the ARTIC-based RSV WGS assay enables near real-time surveillance and strengthens data-driven public health responses to future outbreaks. IMPORTANCE RSV, with two major subtypes, RSV-A and RSV-B, causes acute respiratory infections that can be severe in infants under 6 months and older adults. Current RSV surveillance at the GPHL relies on the Thermo Fisher TaqMan Gene Expression Capillary assay, which detects and subtypes RSV but lacks resolution for lineage classification and identification of emerging variants. To address this critical gap, GPHL developed and evaluated an amplicon-based WGS assay using 214 de-identified RSV clinical specimens. Genomes were amplified using ARTIC-style and custom-primer sets, with ARTIC primers showing superior performance. analysis.study_design_and_population: The Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) developed and evaluated an amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing (WGS) assay for RSV surveillance. A total of 214 de-identified remnant clinical specimens (102 RSV-A and 112 RSV-B) with RT-PCR C q values <31 were included.
analysis.methods: RSV genomes were amplified using ARTIC-style and custom primer sets, with the ARTIC set showing superior performance. Libraries were prepared using a modified Illumina COVIDSeq protocol, sequenced on NextSeq 1000/2000 instruments, and analyzed using the GPHL-RSV-PIPE bioinformatics pipeline.
analysis.main_results: Among genomes meeting validation criteria, sequencing depth was slightly higher for RSV-A (median 53,433×; mean 51,076×) than RSV-B (median 49,699×; mean 46,945×), whereas genomic coverage was slightly lower for RSV-A (median 97.5%; mean 96.6%) than RSV-B (median 98.3%; mean 97.6%). Specificity testing of 31 non-RSV specimens produced no false-positive detections.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The assay demonstrated strong sequencing depth, genomic coverage, specificity, repeatability, reproducibility, and low limits of detection. These results establish that the ARTIC-based WGS assay enables near real-time genomic surveillance, supporting monitoring of circulating RSV strains and informing data-driven public health responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the implementation of near real-time genomic surveillance for RSV, which can inform public health responses to future outbreaks and improve the monitoring of circulating strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the development and evaluation of an ARTIC-based amplicon sequencing assay for whole-genome characterization of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). RSV, a negative-sense RNA virus, causes acute respiratory infections in infants and older adults, with two subtypes, RSV-A and RSV-B, evolving rapidly. The Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) created a new assay to address the limitations of current methods, which lack resolution for lineage classification and identification of emerging variants. The assay was tested on 214 de-identified clinical specimens, with RSV-A and RSV-B genomes amplified using ARTIC-style and custom primer sets. The ARTIC set showed superior performance, and the results demonstrated strong sequencing depth, genomic coverage, specificity, repeatability, reproducibility, and low limits of detection. The assay enables near real-time genomic surveillance, which can support monitoring of circulating RSV strains and inform data-driven public health responses. The study does not report specific limitations of the design, but the results suggest a high level of confidence in the assay's performance.

title_zh: 基于ARTIC的扩增子测序检测方法的开发与评估用于基因组的全基因组表征。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a ~15.2 kb negative-sense RNA virus, causes acute respiratory infections in infants and older adults. Its two subtypes, RSV-A and RSV-B, evolve rapidly, making ongoing monitoring of circulating strains essential. The Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) developed and evaluated an amplicon-based whole-genome sequencing (WGS) assay for RSV surveillance. A total of 214 de-identified remnant clinical specimens (102 RSV-A and 112 RSV-B) with RT-PCR C q values <31 were included. RSV genomes were amplified using ARTIC-style and custom primer sets, with the ARTIC set showing superior performance. Libraries were prepared using a modified Illumina COVIDSeq protocol, sequenced on NextSeq 1000/2000 instruments, and analyzed using the GPHL-RSV-PIPE bioinformatics pipeline. Among genomes meeting validation criteria, sequencing depth was slightly higher for RSV-A (median 53,433×; mean 51,076×) than RSV-B (median 49,699×; mean 46,945×), whereas genomic coverage was slightly lower for RSV-A (median 97.5%; mean 96.6%) than RSV-B (median 98.3%; mean 97.6%). Predominant lineages were A.D.3.1 and A.D.5.2 for RSV-A and B.D.E.1 for RSV-B. For RSV-A, the assay showed 92.8% accuracy, 96.2% sensitivity, 87.2% specificity, 92.6% positive predictive value, and 93.2% negative predictive value. Intra- and inter-run precision assessed using 16 and 53-57 genomes, respectively, showed nearly 100% consensus genome identity with 0–5 nucleotide differences. Specificity testing of 31 non-RSV specimens produced no false-positive detections. Limits of detection were 4.4 TCID 50 /mL for RSV-A and 18.6 TCID 50 /mL for RSV-B. These results demonstrate that the ARTIC-based RSV WGS assay enables near real-time surveillance and strengthens data-driven public health responses to future outbreaks. IMPORTANCE RSV, with two major subtypes, RSV-A and RSV-B, causes acute respiratory infections that can be severe in infants under 6 months and older adults. Current RSV surveillance at the GPHL relies on the Thermo Fisher TaqMan Gene Expression Capillary assay, which detects and subtypes RSV but lacks resolution for lineage classification and identification of emerging variants. To address this critical gap, GPHL developed and evaluated an amplicon-based WGS assay using 214 de-identified RSV clinical specimens. Genomes were amplified using ARTIC-style and custom-primer sets, with ARTIC primers showing superior performance. The assay demonstrated strong sequencing depth, genomic coverage, specificity, repeatability, reproducibility, and low limits of detection. RSV lineages were accurately determined based on genetic variation. These results establish that the ARTIC-based WGS assay enables near real-time genomic surveillance, supporting monitoring of circulating RSV strains and informing data-driven public health responses.
abstract_zh: 摘要 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是一种约 15.2 kb 的负义 RNA 病毒,可引起婴儿和老年人的急性呼吸道感染。它的两种亚型 RSV-A 和 RSV-B 进化迅速,因此对流行菌株的持续监测至关重要。乔治亚州公共卫生实验室 (GPHL) 开发并评估了基于扩增子的 RSV 基因组 测序 (WGS) 检测方法。总共纳入了 214 份未鉴定的残留临床标本(102 份 RSV-A 和 112 份 RSV-B),其 RT-PCR C q 值<31。RSV 基因组 使用 ARTIC 型和定制引物组进行扩增,ARTIC 组显示出卓越的性能。使用修改后的 Illumina COVIDSeq 方案制备文库,在 NextSeq 1000/2000 仪器上进行测序,并使用 GPHL-RSV-PIPE 生物信息学流程进行分析。在符合验证标准的 基因组 中,RSV-A 的测序深度(中位数 53,433×;平均值 51,076×)略高于 RSV-B(中位数 49,699×;平均值 46,945×),而 RSV-A 的基因组覆盖度(中位数 97.5%;平均值 96.6%)略低于 RSV-B(中位数 98.3%;平均值 96.6%)。平均 97.6%)。RSV-A 的主要谱系为 A.D.3.1 和 A.D.5.2,RSV-B 的主要谱系为 B.D.E.1。对于 RSV-A,该测定显示出 92.8% 的准确度、96.2% 的灵敏度、87.2% 的特异性、92.6% 的阳性预测值和 93.2% 的阴性预测值。分别使用 16 和 53-57 基因组 评估的运行内和运行间精度显示,基因组 一致性接近 100%,存在 0-5 个核苷酸差异。对 31 个非 RSV 样本的特异性测试未产生假阳性检测。RSV-A 的检测限为 4.4 TCID 50 /mL,RSV-B 的检测限为 18.6 TCID 50 /mL。这些结果表明,基于 ARTIC 的 RSV WGS 检测可实现近乎实时的 监测,并加强对未来 暴发 的数据驱动的公共卫生响应。重要性 RSV 有两种主要亚型:RSV-A 和 RSV-B,可引起急性呼吸道感染,对于 6 个月以下的婴儿和老年人可能会造成严重感染。目前 GPHL 的 RSV 监测 依赖于 Thermo Fisher TaqMan 基因表达毛细管检测,该检测可检测 RSV 并确定其亚型,但缺乏谱系分类和新出现变异鉴定的分辨率。为了解决这一关键差距,广药集团使用 214 个去识别的 RSV 临床标本开发并评估了一种基于扩增子的 WGS 检测方法。基因组 使用 ARTIC 型和定制引物组进行扩增,ARTIC 引物表现出卓越的性能。该测定显示出强大的测序深度、基因组覆盖度、特异性、重复性、再现性和低检测限。根据遗传变异准确确定RSV谱系。这些结果表明,基于 ARTIC 的 WGS 检测可实现近乎实时的 基因组监测,支持监测循环 RSV 毒株并为数据驱动的公共卫生应对措施提供信息。

title: Seroprevalence and Molecular Characterisation of Human Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Infections in Children at a Tertiary Care Centre in Rural Maharashtra, India.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the foremost viral cause of acute lower respiratory infections (ALRIs) in children under five years of age, yet surveillance data from rural India remain conspicuously scarce. This cross-sectional study simultaneously characterised RSV seroprevalence and active molecular infection in two non-overlapping paediatric cohorts from Karad, Maharashtra, India (September 2021-August 2023). In Cohort 1 (serological study, n = 290; ≥246 required by a prior calculation), RSV-specific immunoglobulin M (IgM) antibodies were detected in 182 children (62.8%) by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA; indirect format with rheumatoid factor pre-absorption), with the highest positivity in the 2-3-year age group. This rate is interpreted as an indicator of high community-level RSV exposure rather than a precise incidence estimate, given the known limitations of single-timepoint IgM testing in previously exposed children. In Cohort 2 (molecular study, n = 283; ≥233 required), RSV-B was detected by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) in 7 of 283 (2.47%) symptomatic children presenting with acute respiratory infection (ARI) or severe ARI (SARI); no RSV-A was identified. The low detection rate is consistent with pandemic-era suppression of respiratory virus transmission. All seven RSV-B strains belonged to the GB5 genotype and formed a phylogenetically distinct local sub-cluster within global GB5 (82% bootstrap support), carrying shared amino acid substitutions in glycoprotein G (A74V, I252T, 165del) and fusion protein F (F12I, S190N, S211N, S389P), numbered relative to the GISAID reference sequence EPI_ISL_1653999 (F precursor). Substitutions S190N and S211N map to the apex region of prefusion F at or adjacent to antigenic site Ø-the primary binding epitope for nirsevimab-though their functional impact on neutralisation was not assessed in vitro and requires dedicated experimental evaluation. A novel predicted N-linked glycosylation site at position F180 was identified in one strain (KIMS-102/2022), with potential but unconfirmed implications for local immune evasion. RSV-B illness was predominantly mild. These findings provide the first combined serological and molecular RSV dataset from rural Maharashtra and underscore the need for region-specific surveillance as RSV prophylactics become available in India.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to characterise RSV seroprevalence and molecular infection in children from rural Maharashtra, India. A cross-sectional design was used, involving two non-overlapping cohorts: one for serological analysis and another for molecular detection. In the serological cohort, 62.8% of children showed RSV-specific IgM antibodies, with the highest positivity in the 2-3-year age group. In the molecular cohort, RSV-B was detected in 2.47% of symptomatic children, while no RSV-A was identified. The low detection rate was attributed to pandemic-era suppression of respiratory virus transmission. All RSV-B strains belonged to the GB5 genotype, forming a local sub-cluster with specific amino acid substitutions. A novel predicted N-linked glycosylation site was identified in one strain, though its functional impact on immune evasion remains unconfirmed. The study highlights the need for region-specific surveillance as RSV prophylactics become available in India, but the findings are limited by the absence of in vitro functional assessments of the identified substitutions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是五岁以下儿童急性下呼吸道感染 (ALRI) 的首要病毒原因,但来自印度农村地区的 呼吸道合胞病毒 数据仍然明显匮乏。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项横断面研究同时对来自印度马哈拉施特拉邦卡拉德的两名非重叠儿科 队列研究 的 RSV 血清流行率 和活性分子感染进行了表征(2021 年 9 月至 2023 年 8 月)。
elements_zh.methods: 在队列研究 1(血清学研究,n = 290;根据先前计算要求≥246)中,通过酶联免疫吸附测定(ELISA;类风湿因子预吸收的间接格式)在182名儿童(62.8%)中检测到RSV特异性免疫球蛋白M(IgM)抗体,其中2-3岁年龄组的阳性率最高。
elements_zh.main_results: 在群体2(分子研究,n = 283;需≥233例)中,通过实时逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)在283名患有急性呼吸道感染(ARI)或严重ARI(SARI)的有症状儿童中检测到7例(2.47%)RSV-B;未检测到RSV-A。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 低检出率与大流行时期呼吸道病毒 传播 的抑制一致。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现提供了马哈拉施特拉邦农村地区第一个组合的血清学和分子 RSV 数据集,并强调了随着 RSV 预防药物在印度的普及,对特定地区 监测 的需求。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据没有报告已确定的氨基酸取代对中和的功能影响的详细评估。

title: Matrilysin (MMP-7) Restricts RSV Infection and Airway Inflammation through Proteolysis of CCR3 and RSV-G
abstract: Airway epithelium forms a frontline barrier against microbial invasion through mucociliary clearance and the secretion of antimicrobial and immunomodulatory mediators. Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), traditionally viewed as tissue-remodelling enzymes, are also implicated in inflammatory processes and are recognized for their capacity to shap host-pathogen interactions. This study investigates the role of MMP-7 (matrilysin) in airway inflammation and the pathogenesis of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. In silico analyses predicted that MMP-7 binds CCR3, the receptor for eotaxin-1/CCL11, and that it also engages the region of the RSV G protein that docks onto CCR3, pointing to a shared biochemical mechanism interfering with both chemokine binding and viral attachment. Mechanistically, MMP-7 proteolytically cleaved CCR3, disrupting eotaxin-1/CCL11 binding and reducing eosinophil activation and chemotaxis, whereas CX3CR1 was unaffected. Importantly, biophysical measurements confirmed that MMP-7 binds and cleaves the RSV G protein, consequently restricting RSV entry and replication in airway epithelial cells. In vivo, MMP-7-deficient mice displayed higher RSV infection, exacerbated airway inflammation and increased mucus production following RSV challenge. Collectively, these findings identify MMP-7 as a key epithelial antiviral effector coordinating both antiviral defense and the regulation of pulmonary inflammation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study investigates the role of MMP-7 in airway inflammation and the pathogenesis of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. The research is motivated by the need to understand how airway epithelium defends against microbial invasion through mucociliary clearance and the secretion of antimicrobial and immunomodulatory mediators.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed in vivo experiments using MMP-7-deficient mice to examine the effects of RSV challenge on infection levels, airway inflammation and mucus production. The research was conducted in a laboratory setting with a focus on airway epithelial cells.
analysis.methods: The study used in silico analyses to predict MMP-7 interactions with CCR3 and the RSV G protein, followed by biophysical measurements to confirm these interactions. In vivo experiments involved assessing RSV infection, airway inflammation and mucus production in MMP-7-deficient mice.
analysis.main_results: In vivo, MMP-7-deficient mice displayed higher RSV infection, exacerbated airway inflammation and increased mucus production following RSV challenge.

title_zh: Matrilysin (MMP-7) 通过 CCR3 和 RSV-G 的蛋白水解来限制 RSV 感染和气道炎症
source_body_en: Airway epithelium forms a frontline barrier against microbial invasion through mucociliary clearance and the secretion of antimicrobial and immunomodulatory mediators. Matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), traditionally viewed as tissue-remodelling enzymes, are also implicated in inflammatory processes and are recognized for their capacity to shap host-pathogen interactions. This study investigates the role of MMP-7 (matrilysin) in airway inflammation and the pathogenesis of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. In silico analyses predicted that MMP-7 binds CCR3, the receptor for eotaxin-1/CCL11, and that it also engages the region of the RSV G protein that docks onto CCR3, pointing to a shared biochemical mechanism interfering with both chemokine binding and viral attachment. Mechanistically, MMP-7 proteolytically cleaved CCR3, disrupting eotaxin-1/CCL11 binding and reducing eosinophil activation and chemotaxis, whereas CX3CR1 was unaffected. Importantly, biophysical measurements confirmed that MMP-7 binds and cleaves the RSV G protein, consequently restricting RSV entry and replication in airway epithelial cells. In vivo, MMP-7-deficient mice displayed higher RSV infection, exacerbated airway inflammation and increased mucus production following RSV challenge. Collectively, these findings identify MMP-7 as a key epithelial antiviral effector coordinating both antiviral defense and the regulation of pulmonary inflammation.
abstract_zh: 气道上皮通过黏液纤毛清除作用和分泌抗菌及免疫调节介质,形成抵御微生物入侵的第一道防线。基质金属蛋白酶(MMPs),传统上被视为组织重塑酶,也参与炎症过程,并被认识到其能够影响呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染中气道上皮与病原体的相互作用。本研究探讨了MMP-7(基质金属蛋白酶-7)在气道炎症及呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染中的作用。计算机模拟分析预测MMP-7能够结合CCR3受体(eotaxin-1/CCL11的受体),并且还能结合RSV G蛋白与CCR3结合的区域,提示存在一种共同的生化机制,干扰化学引诱素结合和病毒附着。从机制上看,MMP-7通过蛋白酶活性切割CCR3,从而破坏eotaxin-1/CCL11的结合,减少嗜酸性粒细胞的激活和趋化作用,而CX3CR1则不受影响。重要的是,生物物理测量证实MMP-7能够结合并切割RSV G蛋白,从而限制RSV在气道上皮细胞中的进入和复制。在体内实验中,MMP-7缺失的小鼠在RSV感染后表现出更高的感染水平、更严重的气道炎症和增加的黏液分泌。综上所述,这些发现确定了MMP-7作为关键的气道上皮效应因子,协调气道防御和肺部炎症的调控。

title: Clinical Impact of Acute Respiratory Virus Infections in Nursing Home Residents.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the suspected acute respiratory infection (ARI) risk and the clinical impact of a range of respiratory viruses in Dutch nursing home (NH) residents. DESIGN: Prospective cohort study (March 2023-May 2025). SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Residents from 15 Dutch NHs were enrolled when suspected of an ARI. METHODS: Clinical data were collected on days 0, 14, and 28. Residual nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs were tested for a broad respiratory virus panel. A Bayesian multilevel logistic model including seasonal and NH-level random effects estimated suspected ARI risk. Relative clinical outcomes were compared by virus. RESULTS: Among 3195 residents, 526 suspected ARI episodes occurred. The estimated suspected ARI risk was 10.2% (95% credible interval, 1.7-43.8). Viruses were identified in 291 episodes: severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2; 29.0%), influenza A virus (23.6%), rhinovirus/enterovirus (18.8%), respiratory syncytial virus (11.8%), human metapneumovirus (hMPV; 6.4%), parainfluenza viruses (5.1%), and human coronaviruses (5.4%). hMPV and respiratory syncytial virus tended to be associated with higher odds of moderate or severe disease, and hMPV was linked to a 4-fold increase in bed hours. Influenza A was associated with delayed recovery, oxygen requirement, and a 3-fold risk of secondary bacterial pneumonia. SARS-CoV-2 cases had higher estimated odds of recovery by day 14 and spent fewer additional hours in bed during ARI episodes. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Influenza remains a major contributor to ARI burden in NH residents, whereas SARS-CoV-2 has relatively limited impact. The pronounced clinical impact of hMPV suggests its relevance for ARI management in this population.
journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association

title: Evaluation of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F IgG Antibodies in Japanese Mother–Infant Pairs Following Maternal Abrysvo Vaccination and in Infants Hospitalized with RSV Infection
abstract: Background/Objectives: The approval of Abrysvo, a maternal bivalent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F (pre-F) vaccine, marked a major milestone in pediatric prophylaxis. However, real-world serological data on transplacental antibody transfer in Asian populations remains limited. This brief report evaluated serum RSV pre-F immunoglobulin G (IgG) geometric mean titers (GMTs) across three distinct Japanese cohorts. Methods: This single-center, comparative study analyzed neonates born to Abrysvo-vaccinated mothers (n = 12), neonates born to unvaccinated mothers (n = 40), and infants aged <6 months hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection (n = 18) using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Results: Neonates of vaccinated mothers exhibited significantly higher pre-F IgG GMTs (4.74; 95% CI: 4.30–5.18) than those of unvaccinated mothers (3.80; 95% CI: 3.50–4.14). Conversely, infants requiring hospitalization for RSV infection demonstrated critically low pre-F IgG GMTs (1.08; 95% CI: 0.65–2.15), revealing statistically significant differences across all three groups (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Maternal immunization with Abrysvo significantly enhances passive humoral immunity in Japanese neonates compared to natural background immunity. Given the severe antibody deficiency observed in hospitalized infants, expanding maternal vaccination coverage is a high-priority public health strategy to mitigate the pediatric RSV burden in the post-pandemic era.

abstract_original: Background/Objectives: The approval of Abrysvo, a maternal bivalent respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F (pre-F) vaccine, marked a major milestone in pediatric prophylaxis. However, real-world serological data on transplacental antibody transfer in Asian populations remains limited. This brief report evaluated serum RSV pre-F immunoglobulin G (IgG) geometric mean titers (GMTs) across three distinct Japanese cohorts. Methods: This single-center, comparative study analyzed neonates born to Abrysvo-vaccinated mothers (n = 12), neonates born to unvaccinated mothers (n = 40), and infants aged <6 months hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection (n = 18) using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Results: Neonates of vaccinated mothers exhibited significantly higher pre-F IgG GMTs (4.74; 95% CI: 4.30–5.18) than those of unvaccinated mothers (3.80; 95% CI: 3.50–4.14). Conversely, infants requiring hospitalization for RSV infection demonstrated critically low pre-F IgG GMTs (1.08; 95% CI: 0.65–2.15), revealing statistically significant differences across all three groups (p < 0.001). Conclusions: Maternal immunization with Abrysvo significantly enhances passive humoral immunity in Japanese neonates compared to natural background immunity. Given the severe antibody deficiency observed in hospitalized infants, expanding maternal vaccination coverage is a high-priority public health strategy to mitigate the pediatric RSV burden in the post-pandemic era.
title_original: Evaluation of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F IgG Antibodies in Japanese Mother–Infant Pairs Following Maternal Abrysvo Vaccination and in Infants Hospitalized with RSV Infection

abstract_zh: 背景/目标:Abrysvo 的批准是一种母体二价 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 预输注 F (pre-F) 疫苗,标志着儿科预防的一个重要里程碑。然而,亚洲人群经胎盘抗体转移的真实血清学数据仍然有限。这份简短的报告评估了三种不同的日本 队列研究 的血清 RSV pre-F 免疫球蛋白 G (IgG) 几何平均滴度 (GMT)。方法:这项单中心比较研究使用酶联免疫吸附测定 (ELISA) 分析了接种 Abrysvo 疫苗的母亲所生的新生儿 (n = 12)、未接种疫苗的母亲所生的新生儿 (n = 40) 以及因实验室确诊的 RSV 感染而住院的 6 个月以下婴儿 (n = 18)。结果:接种疫苗的母亲的新生儿表现出比未接种疫苗的母亲 (3.80;95% CI: 3.50–4.14) 显着更高的前 F IgG GMT (4.74;95% CI: 4.30–5.18)。相反,因 RSV 感染而需要住院治疗的婴儿表现出极低的 pre-F IgG GMT(1.08;95% CI:0.65–2.15),显示所有三组之间存在统计学显着差异(p < 0.001)。结论:与自然背景免疫相比,Abrysvo 母体免疫显着增强了日本新生儿的被动体液免疫。鉴于住院婴儿中观察到的严重抗体缺乏症,扩大孕产妇 疫苗接种 覆盖范围是减轻大流行后时代儿科 RSV 负担的一项高度优先的公共卫生战略。

title: Detection of nirsevimab-resistant RSV-B variants in children carrying the F:N201T substitution through genomic surveillance, Spain, 2025/26 season
abstract: During Spain's 2025/26 RSV season, three children were infected with RSV-B viruses carrying the F protein N201T substitution. Two who received nirsevimab that season were hospitalised (one required intensive care); the third was treated previously. Recombinant expression studies confirmed reduced nirsevimab recognition. Genomic data indicated sporadic emergence across distinct RSV-B backgrounds rather than expansion of a single lineage. Findings highlight the importance of combining genomic surveillance with antigenic characterisation to detect and interpret variants with reduced susceptibility to antibody-based prevention.

title: Construction and application of a novel respiratory syncytial virus vaccine based on Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron outer membrane vesicles
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, young children, immunocompromised adults, and elderly individuals with comorbidities. Its high pathogenicity and associated mortality impose a substantial disease burden on public health. Vaccination represents a key strategy for preventing RSV infection. However, currently approved RSV vaccines exhibit limitations. For instance, Abrysvo and Arexvy pose potential safety risks in clinical use, and the long-term protective efficacy of mRESVIA may wane over time. Therefore, this article proposes and explores a novel RSV vaccine strategy utilizing Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron outer membrane vesicles (Bt OMVs) as a delivery platform. This strategy capitalizes on the unique advantages of Bt OMVs, including efficient mucosal delivery, low inherent toxicity, and targeted modulation of T cell homeostasis—specifically enhancing Treg and Th1 responses while suppressing excessive Th2 and Th17 activation, which serves as the core mechanism for preventing vaccine-enhanced disease (VED)—to effectively present the RSV F protein antigen. It offers a novel approach to develop next-generation RSV vaccines that combine durable protection with enhanced clinical safety.

title_zh: 基于多形拟杆菌外膜囊泡的新型呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗的构建及应用
source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, young children, immunocompromised adults, and elderly individuals with comorbidities. Its high pathogenicity and associated mortality impose a substantial disease burden on public health. Vaccination represents a key strategy for preventing RSV infection. However, currently approved RSV vaccines exhibit limitations. For instance, Abrysvo and Arexvy pose potential safety risks in clinical use, and the long-term protective efficacy of mRESVIA may wane over time. Therefore, this article proposes and explores a novel RSV vaccine strategy utilizing Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron outer membrane vesicles (Bt OMVs) as a delivery platform. This strategy capitalizes on the unique advantages of Bt OMVs, including efficient mucosal delivery, low inherent toxicity, and targeted modulation of T cell homeostasis—specifically enhancing Treg and Th1 responses while suppressing excessive Th2 and Th17 activation, which serves as the core mechanism for preventing vaccine-enhanced disease (VED)—to effectively present the RSV F protein antigen. It offers a novel approach to develop next-generation RSV vaccines that combine durable protection with enhanced clinical safety.

title: Transcriptional signatures of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection using relaxed magnitude altitude score with hub-centric network analysis (RMAS-HCNA)
abstract: Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus A (RSVA) and respiratory syncytial virus B (RSVB) may induce distinct airway host responses. We compared them with influenza A virus (IAV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in airway organ tissue equivalents (OTEs) and developed the Relaxed Magnitude Altitude Score with Hub-Centric Network Analysis framework (RMAS-HCNA). Methods OTEs were infected with RSVA-GFP5 or RSVB-GFP3 at low multiplicity of infection and profiled at 24 and 72 h using the NanoString nCounter Host Response Panel. Previous IAV and hMPV profiles were integrated. Analyses included source-matched differential expression, cross-virus ranking, network-based module selection, nested cross-validation, and Gene Ontology Biological Process enrichment. Results RSVA showed the strongest temporal expansion and developed a late response centered on intracellular transport, localization, and organelle organization. RSVB remained the most restricted response, shifting from early inflammatory and signaling-associated activity to a later interferon-stimulated profile. IAV maintained a broad antiviral response, whereas hMPV combined limited induction with extensive late downregulation of stress, catabolic, metabolic, and transport-related processes. A shared antiviral component was present across infections, while downregulated responses were largely virus dependent. Under five-fold outer and four-fold inner nested cross-validation, the selected genes achieved a mean outer-test Macro F1 of 0.859 and balanced accuracy of 0.888, compared with 0.604 and 0.616 for the all-gene comparator. Discussion The four viruses shared an antiviral foundation but followed distinct temporal and functional trajectories. The framework identified compact, biologically representative panels that generalized better than the complete measured gene set, although independent genome-wide and in vivo validation remains necessary.

title_zh: 使用宽松的海拔高度评分和以中心为中心的网络分析 (RMAS-HCNA) 的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染的转录特征
source_body_en: Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus A (RSVA) and respiratory syncytial virus B (RSVB) may induce distinct airway host responses. We compared them with influenza A virus (IAV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in airway organ tissue equivalents (OTEs) and developed the Relaxed Magnitude Altitude Score with Hub-Centric Network Analysis framework (RMAS-HCNA). Methods OTEs were infected with RSVA-GFP5 or RSVB-GFP3 at low multiplicity of infection and profiled at 24 and 72 h using the NanoString nCounter Host Response Panel. Previous IAV and hMPV profiles were integrated. Analyses included source-matched differential expression, cross-virus ranking, network-based module selection, nested cross-validation, and Gene Ontology Biological Process enrichment. Results RSVA showed the strongest temporal expansion and developed a late response centered on intracellular transport, localization, and organelle organization. RSVB remained the most restricted response, shifting from early inflammatory and signaling-associated activity to a later interferon-stimulated profile. IAV maintained a broad antiviral response, whereas hMPV combined limited induction with extensive late downregulation of stress, catabolic, metabolic, and transport-related processes. A shared antiviral component was present across infections, while downregulated responses were largely virus dependent. Under five-fold outer and four-fold inner nested cross-validation, the selected genes achieved a mean outer-test Macro F1 of 0.859 and balanced accuracy of 0.888, compared with 0.604 and 0.616 for the all-gene comparator. Discussion The four viruses shared an antiviral foundation but followed distinct temporal and functional trajectories. The framework identified compact, biologically representative panels that generalized better than the complete measured gene set, although independent genome-wide and in vivo validation remains necessary.
abstract_zh: 简介 呼吸道合胞病毒 A (RSVA) 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 B (RSVB) 可能会引起不同的气道 宿主 反应。我们将它们与甲型流感病毒 (IAV) 和人类偏肺病毒 (hMPV) 的气道器官组织等效物 (OTE) 进行比较,并使用以枢纽为中心的网络分析框架 (RMAS-HCNA) 开发了松弛幅度高度评分。方法 OTE 以低感染复数感染 RSVA-GFP5 或 RSVB-GFP3,并使用 NanoString nCounter 宿主 响应面板在 24 小时和 72 小时进行分析。集成了以前的 IAV 和 hMPV 配置文件。分析包括源匹配差异表达、交叉病毒排序、基于网络的模块选择、嵌套交叉验证和基因本体生物过程富集。结果 RSVA 显示出最强的时间扩展,并产生以细胞内运输、定位和细胞器组织为中心的晚期反应。RSVB 仍然是最受限制的反应,从早期炎症和信号相关活动转变为后来的干扰素刺激谱。IAV 维持广泛的 抗病毒药物 反应,而 hMPV 将有限的诱导与应激、分解代谢、代谢和运输相关过程的广泛后期下调结合起来。感染过程中存在共同的 抗病毒药物 成分,而下调的反应很大程度上依赖于病毒。在五重外部和四重内部嵌套交叉验证下,所选基因的平均外部测试宏 F1 为 0.859,平衡精度为 0.888,而全基因比较器的平衡精度为 0.604 和 0.616。讨论 这四种病毒共享 抗病毒药物 基础,但遵循不同的时间和功能轨迹。尽管仍然需要独立的 基因组 范围和体内验证,但该框架确定了紧凑的、具有生物学代表性的面板,其概括性优于完整的测量基因集。

title: Concurrent Sigmoid Microperforation in the Setting of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection in an Adult Patient: A Case Report
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common respiratory pathogen primarily associated with pediatric infections; however, RSV infection is recognized as a significant cause of illness in adults, particularly during winter months.Despite its well-established association with respiratory disease, RSV can also present with extrapulmonary manifestations, including gastrointestinal symptoms.Here, we present the case of a 65-year-old male who presented with dyspnea and abdominal pain and tested positive for RSV.Concurrently, the patient was discovered to have a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis on abdominal imaging.Surgical intervention was deferred due to a high perioperative risk, and the patient was treated conservatively with broad-spectrum antibiotics.Shortly after, the patient developed multiple abdominal abscesses, which were treated with CT-guided percutaneous drainage and drain placement.RSV has been documented to cause gastrointestinal pathology in children by weakening the bowel wall.As RSV was identified in this patient in the setting of gastrointestinal pathology, it is hypothesized that RSV may have contributed to this patient's gastrointestinal condition.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a common respiratory pathogen primarily associated with pediatric infections; however, RSV infection is recognized as a significant cause of illness in adults, particularly during winter months. Despite its well-established association with respiratory disease, RSV can also present with extrapulmonary manifestations, including gastrointestinal symptoms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study is a case report describing a 65-year-old male patient who presented with dyspnea and abdominal pain and tested positive for RSV. The patient was found to have a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis on abdominal imaging.
analysis.methods: The patient was tested for RSV and underwent abdominal imaging to identify gastrointestinal pathology. Surgical intervention was deferred due to a high perioperative risk, and the patient was treated conservatively with broad-spectrum antibiotics. Subsequently, the patient developed multiple abdominal abscesses, which were managed with CT-guided percutaneous drainage and drain placement.
analysis.main_results: The patient tested positive for RSV and was found to have a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis on abdominal imaging. He developed multiple abdominal abscesses, which were treated with CT-guided percutaneous drainage and drain placement.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: It is hypothesized that RSV may have contributed to the patient's gastrointestinal condition, as RSV has been documented to cause gastrointestinal pathology in children by weakening the bowel wall.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case report highlights the potential for RSV to cause extrapulmonary manifestations, including gastrointestinal complications, in adults, which may inform broader surveillance and diagnostic approaches for RSV-related conditions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a single case report, which limits the generalizability of the findings. However, the evidence is based on direct clinical observations and documented treatment outcomes, supporting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 65-year-old male patient with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection who also presented with a perforated sigmoid diverticulitis and multiple abdominal abscesses. The patient was treated conservatively with broad-spectrum antibiotics and later underwent CT-guided percutaneous drainage for the abscesses. The case suggests that RSV may contribute to gastrointestinal complications in adults, expanding the understanding of its extrapulmonary manifestations. While the study is limited to a single case, it provides valuable insights into the potential for RSV to affect non-respiratory systems, which could inform future research and clinical practices. The findings emphasize the need for broader consideration of RSV in adult patients presenting with gastrointestinal symptoms, particularly during winter months.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究是 病例报告,描述了一名 65 岁男性患者,该患者出现呼吸困难和腹痛,RSV 检测呈阳性。腹部影像学检查发现患者患有穿孔性乙状结肠憩室炎。
elements_zh.methods: 该患者接受了 RSV 检测,并进行了腹部影像学检查,以确定胃肠道病理。由于围手术期风险较高,推迟了手术干预,患者接受了广谱抗生素保守治疗。随后,患者出现多发性腹部脓肿,采用 CT 引导下经皮引流和引流管治疗。
elements_zh.main_results: 该患者RSV检测呈阳性,腹部影像学检查发现乙状结肠憩室炎穿孔。他出现了多发性腹部脓肿,并接受了 CT 引导下经皮引流和引流管放置治疗。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 据推测,RSV 可能导致了患者的胃肠道状况,因为 RSV 已被记录通过削弱肠壁而导致儿童胃肠道病变。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该 病例报告 强调了 RSV 在成人中引起肺外表现(包括胃肠道并发症)的可能性,这可能为更广泛的 病例报告 和 RSV 相关疾病的诊断方法提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是单一的病例报告,这限制了研究结果的普遍性。然而,证据基于直接临床观察和记录的 治疗 结果,支持适度的置信度评估。

title: Respiratory syncytial virus subtype influences pediatric airway microbiome independent of viral burden
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the main cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children. Multiple studies have demonstrated that respiratory microbiome composition is strongly associated with susceptibility to viral infection, disease severity, and subsequent respiratory outcomes. However, it is still unclear how different RSV subtypes affect the respiratory microbiome. Results In this study, we examined the airway microbiome in children infected with RSV-A (n = 18) or RSV-B (n = 12) and compared them with recovered individuals (n = 7) using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing. We found 598 bacterial genera across 39 phyla in 37 samples, with Bacillota , Pseudomonadota , and Actinomycetota being the most common. While overall microbial diversity stayed stable during infection, RSV changed the makeup of the microbial communities, suggesting that infection mainly reorganizes ecological relationships rather than reducing the number of bacterial types. Our analyses showed that the microbiome differed by RSV subtype (PERMANOVA R2 = 0.249, P = 0.016), with RSV-A samples showing more variation than RSV-B. Differential abundance analysis revealed that RSV-A caused greater changes in the microbiome, with 81 affected genera compared to 31 in RSV-B. Viral load did not have a noticeable effect on microbiome structure, as C t values explained only 1.8% of the variation (R2 = 0.018, P = 0.776). Despite these changes, a core group of 45 bacterial genera was found in all groups, including RSV-A, RSV-B, and recovered individuals. Conclusions Our results indicate that RSV subtype is a key factor shaping the respiratory microbiome, more so than viral load, and leads to distinct microbial patterns in the pediatric airway. These findings highlight a previously unrecognized aspect of RSV infection and suggest that differences between subtypes may affect disease progression, immune response, and clinical outcomes.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是婴幼儿严重下呼吸道感染的主要原因。多项研究表明,呼吸道微生物组的组成与病毒感染的易感性、疾病的严重程度和随后的呼吸道结果密切相关。然而,目前尚不清楚不同 RSV 亚型如何影响呼吸道微生物组。结果在本研究中,我们检查了感染 RSV-A (n = 18) 或 RSV-B (n = 12) 的儿童的气道微生物组,并使用全长 16S rRNA 基因测序将其与康复个体 (n = 7) 进行比较。我们在 37 个样本中发现了 39 个门的 598 个细菌属,其中杆菌门、假单胞菌门和放线菌门是最常见的。虽然总体微生物多样性在感染期间保持稳定,但 RSV 改变了微生物群落的构成,这表明感染主要是重组生态关系,而不是减少细菌类型的数量。我们的分析表明,微生物组因 RSV 亚型而异(PERMANOVA R2 = 0.249,P = 0.016),RSV-A 样本比 RSV-B 表现出更多变异。差异丰度分析显示,RSV-A 引起微生物组发生更大的变化,受影响的属有 81 个,而 RSV-B 受影响的属有 31 个。病毒载量对微生物组结构没有明显影响,因为 Ct 值仅解释了 1.8% 的变异(R2 = 0.018,P = 0.776)。尽管有这些变化,在所有群体中都发现了 45 个细菌属的核心群体,包括 RSV-A、RSV-B 和康复个体。结论 我们的结果表明,RSV 亚型是影响呼吸道微生物组的关键因素,其作用比病毒载量更重要,并导致儿科气道中独特的微生物模式。这些发现强调了 RSV 感染以前未被认识的一个方面,并表明亚型之间的差异可能会影响疾病进展、免疫应答 和临床结果。

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

title: Etiology and Clinical Manifestations of Acute Respiratory Infections in Pediatric Patients: A Retrospective Study in Moscow, Russia
abstract: Background/Objectives: Acute respiratory viral infections (ARVIs) are the leading cause of pediatric morbidity and exhibit considerable clinical heterogeneity. The analysis of clinical and etiological associations, as well as the identification of factors linked to severe ARVI cases, is essential for effective epidemiological surveillance. Methods: A retrospective, single-center observational study was conducted including 1362 non-COVID-19 pediatric cases of acute respiratory infections (ARIs), registered between 2021 and 2024. Viral pathogens were detected using real-time PCR for broad-spectrum screening of respiratory viruses. Results: Viral etiology was established in approximately 50% of cases. abstract_zh: 背景/目标:急性呼吸道病毒感染(ARVI)是儿科发病的主要原因,并表现出相当大的临床异质性。分析临床和病因学关联,以及识别与严重 ARVI 病例相关的因素,对于有效的流行病学 监测 至关重要。方法:进行了一项回顾性、单中心观察性研究,纳入 2021 年至 2024 年登记的 1362 例非 COVID-19 儿童急性呼吸道感染 (ARIs) 病例。使用实时 PCR 检测病毒病原体,以对呼吸道病毒进行广谱筛查。结果:约 50% 的病例确定了病毒病因。最常检测到的病原体是人鼻病毒(HRV)(35.6%),其次是呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人腺病毒(HAdV)。尽管 HRV 占主导地位,但并未表现出疾病分类学特异性。RSV (OR = 3.2) 和人博卡病毒 (HBoV;OR = 2.4) 与下呼吸道感染的关联性最强,主要属于肺炎类别。RSV 还与支气管炎/毛细支气管炎 相关(OR = 1.8)。流感病毒 (OR = 10.4) 和 HAdV 与上呼吸道感染存在显着相关性,包括鼻咽炎 (OR = 3.88) 和急性扁桃体炎 (OR = 3.9)。此外,HAdV 还与中耳炎相关(OR = 5.1)。在所有临床观察中,有 52.3% 发生严重疾病,最常见于幼儿,特别是与 ZX​​QTERMAQXZ (RSV >80%) 以及人类博卡病毒 (HBoV) 和人类偏肺病毒 (HMPV) (~55-59%) 相关的病例。与单一感染相比,合并感染与疾病严重程度的增加无关(OR = 1.1)。结论:所获得的结果强调了特定病原体对儿童严重呼吸道感染的影响。这些发现支持临床诊断中此类病原体的优先顺序,包括诊断算法的设计和儿科人群患者管理策略的选择。

title: Association between nirsevimab coverage and pediatric emergency department visits for bronchiolitis in 12 European countries: An interrupted time-series analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nirsevimab was introduced to prevent Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infants. Despite its proven effectiveness and similar guidelines across Europe, bronchiolitis reduction varied across Europe. This study explored whether nirsevimab coverage among targeted populations (born in- and out-of-season) was associated to this variability. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We used routinely collected data from 27 pediatric emergency departments across 12 European countries (01/2018-03/2024). All bronchiolitis cases aged <12 months were included. Regions were classified as intervention or control based on nirsevimab implementation. Coverage was obtained from official regional reports. We estimated changes in monthly case using controlled interrupted time-series models accounting for seasonality and temporal trends, by age-groups (0-3 and 3-12 months) and regions during the intervention period (10/2023-03/2024) and examined their correlation to coverage using Pearson's test. Urinary tract infections served as a control outcome. We included 107,088 bronchiolitis cases. Reductions varied widely across regions and age-groups, from +0.6% (95% CI [-9.4, +20.5]) to -61.0% (95% CI [-67.8, -35.2]). Coverage strongly correlated with bronchiolitis reduction across age-groups and regions (ρ = -0.86, p = 0.001). Bronchiolitis trends in control countries remained stable, as did urinary tract infections. As an ecological study, causality cannot be inferred and unmeasured regional differences may have contributed to the variability. CONCLUSIONS: This multinational interrupted time-series analysis identified coverage as a key factor associated to bronchiolitis reduction across age-groups and European regions. Implementation choices across Europe likely influenced coverage, highlighting that nirsevimab benefits depend not only on its intrinsic efficacy, but also on how effectively it is delivered.
authors: Victoria Trenchs Sáinz de la Maza

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between nirsevimab coverage and reductions in pediatric emergency department visits for RSV bronchiolitis across 12 European countries using an interrupted time-series analysis. The research aimed to understand why bronchiolitis reduction varied despite similar guidelines and proven effectiveness of nirsevimab. The study included 107,088 bronchiolitis cases aged <12 months from 27 emergency departments between 2018 and 2024. Using controlled interrupted time-series models, the authors found that bronchiolitis reductions varied widely across regions and age-groups, with coverage strongly correlated with reductions (ρ = -0.86, p = 0.001). They interpreted these findings as indicating that coverage levels were a key factor in bronchiolitis reduction, emphasizing the role of implementation choices. The results suggest that the effectiveness of nirsevimab depends on its coverage and delivery, which has implications for public health strategies. However, the study's ecological design limits the ability to infer causality, and unmeasured regional differences may have influenced the outcomes, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: Changes in Lung Sounds During the Acute Stage of RSV Acute Bronchiolitis in Infants.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Changes in the respiratory function over time in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-induced acute bronchiolitis were evaluated by a lung sound analysis. METHODS: We retrospectively examined changes in lung sound parameters over time in 54 children (median age, 7 months) diagnosed with RSV acute bronchiolitis. We evaluated the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds using a conventional method and analyzed the frequency characteristics of inspiratory sounds using new automated analysis software program. We examined changes in these lung sound parameters over time during and after hospitalization and compared these data with those of age-matched healthy children. RESULTS: In 138 lung sound samples from 54 infants, the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds was greatest within 4 days after the onset and improved over time. In contrast, the greatest changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed at 5 to 10 days after the onset of RSV acute bronchiolitis. Some lung sound parameters in patients with RSV acute bronchiolitis did not return to normal even by 14 days after the onset. CONCLUSIONS: This finding is considered a characteristic of RSV acute bronchiolitis in infants and is meaningful in terms of post-treatment management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate changes in respiratory function over time in RSV-induced acute bronchiolitis, addressing the need to understand the progression of lung sounds in infants with this condition.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study was conducted on 54 children (median age, 7 months) diagnosed with RSV acute bronchiolitis, examining lung sound parameters during and after hospitalization.
analysis.methods: Lung sound parameters were analyzed using both conventional methods and new automated software, with comparisons made to age-matched healthy children's data.
analysis.main_results: In 138 lung sound samples from 54 infants, the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds was greatest within 4 days after onset and improved over time. In contrast, the greatest changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed at 5 to 10 days after onset. Some parameters did not return to normal even by 14 days post-onset.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the dynamic nature of lung sounds in RSV acute bronchiolitis, suggesting that certain parameters may persist beyond the initial recovery phase, which is novel in the context of respiratory sound analysis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the monitoring of respiratory function in infants with RSV bronchiolitis, potentially informing post-treatment management and the timing of clinical assessments.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis and the generalizability of findings. The evidence strength is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated changes in lung sounds during the acute stage of RSV-induced bronchiolitis in infants. By analyzing 138 lung sound samples from 54 children, it found that the power of inspiratory and expiratory sounds peaked within 4 days after onset and improved over time. However, significant changes in inspiratory sound parameters were observed between 5 to 10 days post-onset, and some parameters remained abnormal even by 14 days. The authors interpret these findings as characteristic of RSV bronchiolitis, suggesting their relevance for post-treatment monitoring. The study's retrospective design and reliance on abstract-only evidence limit its depth and generalizability, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估呼吸道合胞病毒(呼吸道合胞病毒)引起的急性毛细支气管炎中呼吸功能随时间的变化,以了解该条件下婴儿肺部声音进展的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对 54 名诊断为急性 RSV 毛细支气管炎 的儿童(中位年龄为 7 个月)进行了一项回顾性研究,检查了住院期间和住院后的肺音参数。
elements_zh.methods: 使用传统方法和新的自动化软件分析肺部声音参数,并与年龄匹配的健康儿童的数据进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 54 名婴儿的 138 个肺音样本中,吸气音和呼气音的力量在发病后 4 天内最强,并随着时间的推移而改善。相比之下,吸气音参数的最大变化出现在发病后 5 至 10 天。即使在发病后 14 天,一些参数也没有恢复正常。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了 RSV 急性 毛细支气管炎 中肺音的动态性质,表明某些参数可能会持续到初始恢复阶段之后,这在呼吸音分析中是新颖的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为监测 RSV 毛细支气管炎 婴儿的呼吸功能提供了见解,可能为 治疗 后的管理和临床评估的时间安排提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是回顾性的,仅基于抽象证据,这可能会限制分析的深度和研究结果的普遍性。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

title: Diversification without convergence: national childhood respiratory pathogen spectra diverge as they diversify, 1990–2023
abstract: BackgroundNational childhood respiratory pathogen spectra are diversifying nearly everywhere -- within-country diversity rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 -- yet whether countries are diversifying toward a common spectrum or along divergent paths is unknown. We quantified between-country compositional distance of national pathogen spectra over the same period. MethodsWe built national pathogen share vectors from Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 lower respiratory infection etiologic attributions (26 pathogens, 204 countries, ages 0-19 years) at five timepoints spanning 1990-2023. Between-country distance was measured as all pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergences (JSD; primary) and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with Baselga and Jaccard decompositions; robustness was assessed across metrics, pathogen panels, low-count thresholds and a balanced panel of 107 countries. ResultsMean pairwise JSD rose from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023 (+238%; trend p = 0.030), peaking in 2021 (+283%) with a partial 2023 pullback. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity rose +120% and the balanced panel +423%. Divergence was entirely balanced variation (share reallocation), with spectrum richness rising from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens. Dispersion rose fastest for influenza (coefficient of variation 0.03 to 0.55) and respiratory syncytial virus (0.08 to 0.48). Within-region distance rose in every computable GBD super-region (five of seven): divergence occurs within regions, not between blocs. ConclusionsNational spectra are re-sorting along country-specific axes as vaccine-preventable dominance recedes at different speeds. Diversification is universal, but convergence is absent: the transition at the etiologic-spectrum level is asynchronous and path-dependent, with implications for empirical treatment policy and pathogen surveillance. Summary boxO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSO_LIEpidemiological transition theory and the global health convergence agenda imply that national cause-of-death structures become more alike as mortality declines, but this expectation has been tested mainly at the level of mortality rates and broad cause groups, not etiologic spectra. C_LIO_LIWithin-country (alpha) diversity of the childhood respiratory pathogen spectrum rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023. C_LI What this study addsO_LIBetween-country (beta) compositional distance roughly tripled over the same period (mean pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergence +238%, 1990 to 2023), robust to distance metric, pathogen panel, COVID-19 exclusion, low-count threshold, and a fixed balanced panel. C_LIO_LIDivergence is driven entirely by reallocation of pathogen shares (balanced variation), is fastest for viral pathogens, and occurs within every GBD super-region, indicating that countries diversify along country-specific paths rather than toward a common spectrum.

title_zh: 多样化但不趋同:国家儿童呼吸道病原体谱随着多样化而出现分歧,1990-2023
source_body_en: BackgroundNational childhood respiratory pathogen spectra are diversifying nearly everywhere -- within-country diversity rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 -- yet whether countries are diversifying toward a common spectrum or along divergent paths is unknown. We quantified between-country compositional distance of national pathogen spectra over the same period. MethodsWe built national pathogen share vectors from Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 lower respiratory infection etiologic attributions (26 pathogens, 204 countries, ages 0-19 years) at five timepoints spanning 1990-2023. Between-country distance was measured as all pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergences (JSD; primary) and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with Baselga and Jaccard decompositions; robustness was assessed across metrics, pathogen panels, low-count thresholds and a balanced panel of 107 countries. ResultsMean pairwise JSD rose from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023 (+238%; trend p = 0.030), peaking in 2021 (+283%) with a partial 2023 pullback. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity rose +120% and the balanced panel +423%. Divergence was entirely balanced variation (share reallocation), with spectrum richness rising from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens. Dispersion rose fastest for influenza (coefficient of variation 0.03 to 0.55) and respiratory syncytial virus (0.08 to 0.48). Within-region distance rose in every computable GBD super-region (five of seven): divergence occurs within regions, not between blocs. ConclusionsNational spectra are re-sorting along country-specific axes as vaccine-preventable dominance recedes at different speeds. Diversification is universal, but convergence is absent: the transition at the etiologic-spectrum level is asynchronous and path-dependent, with implications for empirical treatment policy and pathogen surveillance. Summary boxO_ST_ABSWhat is already known on this topicC_ST_ABSO_LIEpidemiological transition theory and the global health convergence agenda imply that national cause-of-death structures become more alike as mortality declines, but this expectation has been tested mainly at the level of mortality rates and broad cause groups, not etiologic spectra. C_LIO_LIWithin-country (alpha) diversity of the childhood respiratory pathogen spectrum rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023. C_LI What this study addsO_LIBetween-country (beta) compositional distance roughly tripled over the same period (mean pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergence +238%, 1990 to 2023), robust to distance metric, pathogen panel, COVID-19 exclusion, low-count threshold, and a fixed balanced panel. C_LIO_LIDivergence is driven entirely by reallocation of pathogen shares (balanced variation), is fastest for viral pathogens, and occurs within every GBD super-region, indicating that countries diversify along country-specific paths rather than toward a common spectrum.

title: Forecasting viral evolution from phylogenetic trees
abstract: Viral mutation forecasting plays a key role in pandemic preparedness by enabling researchers to anticipate novel variants and design proactive interventions. Evolutionary histories, represented as phylogenetic trees, offer key insights into the emergence of past and present strains, yet their role in predicting future sequence changes remains largely unexplored. We introduce antiGen, a machine learning model that forecasts the evolutionary future of viruses by learning from their evolutionary past. antiGen achieves state-of-the-art performance for predicting mutations to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, anticipating never-before-seen mutations and mutations that emerge years after the model's training window. antiGen-forecasted spike mutations also retain pseudoviral infectivity in vitro. Moreover, antiGen demonstrates leading predictive performance on surface proteins of influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and dengue virus despite far less available sequencing data. Viral evolution models that explicitly learn from phylogenetic structure offer a valuable resource for applications ranging from epidemiological modeling to therapeutic development.

title_zh: 从系统发育树预测病毒 进化
source_body_en: Viral mutation forecasting plays a key role in pandemic preparedness by enabling researchers to anticipate novel variants and design proactive interventions. Evolutionary histories, represented as phylogenetic trees, offer key insights into the emergence of past and present strains, yet their role in predicting future sequence changes remains largely unexplored. We introduce antiGen, a machine learning model that forecasts the evolutionary future of viruses by learning from their evolutionary past. antiGen achieves state-of-the-art performance for predicting mutations to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, anticipating never-before-seen mutations and mutations that emerge years after the model's training window. antiGen-forecasted spike mutations also retain pseudoviral infectivity in vitro. Moreover, antiGen demonstrates leading predictive performance on surface proteins of influenza virus, respiratory syncytial virus, and dengue virus despite far less available sequencing data. Viral evolution models that explicitly learn from phylogenetic structure offer a valuable resource for applications ranging from epidemiological modeling to therapeutic development.

title: RSV Bivalent Prefusion F Protein Vaccine in Pregnancy and Protection Against RSV-Associated Illness in Infants
abstract: Importance The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy has demonstrated efficacy in protecting infants against early-life RSV disease in the pivotal clinical trial. Objective To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize real-world evidence on the effectiveness of RSVpreF in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in infants. Data Sources PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC were searched from January 1, 2020, through January 30, 2026. Study Selection A total of 1144 studies were initially identified. Eligible were nonrandomized studies reporting the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in pregnancy in the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI in infants. Data Extraction and Synthesis All studies were screened independently by 2 reviewers. Data were extracted on RSV-associated outcomes among infants born to women who received RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy and infants born to unvaccinated women. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization. Odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Sidik-Jonkman estimator. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was calculated as (1 − OR) × 100% and assessed in infants from birth to age 3 months and from birth to 6 months, separately. The limited available data precluded meta-analysis of effectiveness against the secondary outcomes of RSV-associated emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death. Results A total of 7 studies were included, comprising 7112 infants, of whom 2684 were born to vaccinated mothers. The studies collected data from January 2024 through April 2025 from Argentina, the UK, and the US. Pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%; 3 studies, 4397 participants; I 2 = 0%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%; 6 studies, 3008 participants; I 2 = 18.7%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. Conclusions and Relevance The results of this systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that postimplementation data support the effectiveness of RSVpreF in pregnancy for the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization during the first 6 months of life. The results support the introduction of RSVpreF into routine antenatal immunization programs.

The central question is whether RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy provides protection against RSV-related illness in infants.

The limited available data precluded meta-analysis of secondary outcomes such as emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the effectiveness of the RSV bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in infants. The target pathogen is respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), specifically RSV-A and RSV-B. The central question is whether RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy provides protection against RSV-related illness in infants.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic review and meta-analysis. Data sources included PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC, searched from January 1, 2020, through January 30, 2026. A total of 1144 studies were initially identified, and all were screened independently by 2 reviewers. The primary outcome was RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization, and odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Sidik-Jonkman estimator. The limited available data precluded meta-analysis of secondary outcomes such as emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. These results suggest that postimplementation data support the effectiveness of RSVpreF in pregnancy for the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization during the first 6 months of life.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the limited available data precluded meta-analysis of effectiveness against secondary outcomes such as RSV-associated emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death. This indicates a gap in the evidence regarding the broader impact of RSVpreF on various RSV-related health outcomes in infants.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The results support the introduction of RSVpreF into routine antenatal immunization programs. Further research is needed to evaluate the vaccine's effectiveness against secondary outcomes and to expand the evidence base with more comprehensive data.

title_zh: RSV 二价预融合 F 蛋白 疫苗 在妊娠期和预防婴儿 RSV 相关疾病中的作用
source_body_en: Importance The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bivalent prefusion F protein vaccine (RSVpreF) administered during pregnancy has demonstrated efficacy in protecting infants against early-life RSV disease in the pivotal clinical trial. Objective To conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize real-world evidence on the effectiveness of RSVpreF in preventing RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI) in infants. Data Sources PubMed, Scopus, and Europe PMC were searched from January 1, 2020, through January 30, 2026. Study Selection A total of 1144 studies were initially identified. Eligible were nonrandomized studies reporting the effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccine in pregnancy in the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI in infants. Data Extraction and Synthesis All studies were screened independently by 2 reviewers. Data were extracted on RSV-associated outcomes among infants born to women who received RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy and infants born to unvaccinated women. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization. Odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis with the Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Sidik-Jonkman estimator. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was calculated as (1 − OR) × 100% and assessed in infants from birth to age 3 months and from birth to 6 months, separately. The limited available data precluded meta-analysis of effectiveness against the secondary outcomes of RSV-associated emergency department visits, intensive care unit admissions, and death. Results A total of 7 studies were included, comprising 7112 infants, of whom 2684 were born to vaccinated mothers. The studies collected data from January 2024 through April 2025 from Argentina, the UK, and the US. Pooled vaccine effectiveness against RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization was 82% (95% CI, 81%-82%; 3 studies, 4397 participants; I 2 = 0%) in infants from birth to 3 months and 78% (95% CI, 70%-84%; 6 studies, 3008 participants; I 2 = 18.7%) in infants from birth to 6 months, when mothers were vaccinated 14 days or more before delivery. Conclusions and Relevance The results of this systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that postimplementation data support the effectiveness of RSVpreF in pregnancy for the prevention of RSV-associated LRTI hospitalization during the first 6 months of life. The results support the introduction of RSVpreF into routine antenatal immunization programs.
